Subject: Renewal + capacity increase request

Hi Stephanie,

We're approaching our annual renewal and would like to expand the Dedicated pool we have with Redwood. Current footprint: 8x A100 reserved, 24/7 with 100k tokens/minute baseline. For Q2–Q3 workload forecast we need to add 4 additional GPUs (A100 class equivalent) and a soft throughput guarantee of 160k tokens/minute during business hours (08:00-20:00 PST).

Can you confirm whether this can be added as an addendum to our renewal (same term) and what the cutover plan looks like? We want minimal disruption — ideally a staged canary and a single coordinated cutover. Procurement will need an estimate of downtime windows and rollback procedures before signing.

Attached: a short spike doc with traffic projections.

Thanks,
Lina Park
Head of Infrastructure
Acme Corp

Subject: Re: Renewal + capacity increase request

Hi Lina — thanks for the note and the projection. We can definitely handle the expansion as an addendum to your renewal. High-level answers up front:

- Yes, add GPUs to your reserved pool under the same renewal term is possible.
- We can guarantee a 160k tokens/min baseline during business hours via config-based throttles and reserved capacity assignment.
- Cutover: we propose a 3-step rollout (dry-run -> canary -> full shift) with a 4-hour maintenance window for final sync, but typical customer-visible disruption is <5 minutes at switch time if DNS/routing handled correctly.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Procurement: sign addendum (we'll send redline-friendly PDF).
2) Ops: schedule two dry-runs next week during off-peak and a final cutover slot the week after.
3) Redwood SRE (Marcus & Monica) to provide runbook and ownership for rollback.

I've looped in Marcus (SRE lead) and Monica (Capacity PM) so they can scope runbook and canary test plan. Victor / Sam — if you have preferred maintenance windows or blackout periods please flag them here.

I'll follow with a proposed cutover timeline and a draft runbook by EOD Monday.

Regards,
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: proposed_pricing_addendum_draft.pdf (pdf)]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 23 Feb 2026 09:08:00 -08:00
Subject: INTERNAL: Cutover runbook outline for ACME addendum

Team — sketching runbook and owners. Putting this here so Stephanie can share a single doc with ACME.

Runbook outline (high level):
- Prep (T-7 days): allocate 4x GPUs to "acme-addendum" reserved pool in staging, validate kernel/quantization profile parity with prod models. Owner: Monica.
- Dry-run 1 (T-5 days, 02:00-04:00 PST): move 10% synthetic traffic using traffic mirror, validate latency/throughput, KV cache behavior. Owner: Marcus.
- Dry-run 2 (T-3 days, 02:00-04:00 PST): repeat with 25% real traffic (non-prod tokens), validate billing meter and autoscaling thresholds. Owner: Marcus.
- Canary (Cutover Day, 10:00-12:00 PST): shift 10% real user traffic to new pool, monitor 15 minutes health windows, metrics: p95_latency, error_rate, token_throughput. Owner: SRE oncall.
- Full shift (Cutover Day, 12:30 PST): ramp to 100% over 30 minutes using weighted routing (10% increments every 3 minutes), monitor for regressions.
- Rollback: weighted routing back to old pool in reverse increments + revoke new pool if any major outage. Time to rollback target: <10 minutes.

Dependencies and notes:
- Need procurement sign-off on price addendum before T-5.
- Schedule change freeze from ACME for 24 hours around Cutover Day (T-0 +/-12h).
- We will provide a read-only link to the runbook and a PagerDuty escalation list.

I'll produce cutover_runbook_v2.md with exact commands, observability queries, and failover steps.

— Marcus
